summary.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 10% YoY to Rs 14.151 bn, but FY26 EBITDA margin fell to 13.7% amid SPP UK service-mix shift and Rs 389 mn labour-code charge.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue grew 10% YoY to Rs 14.151 bn with EBITDA of Rs 2.093 bn (14.8% margin) and PAT of Rs 1.121 bn. Full-year revenue was flat-to-marginally up at Rs 45.380 bn (+1%), with EBITDA of Rs 6.213 bn (13.7%) and PAT of Rs 3.772 bn. Domestic revenue fell 3% for FY26 while Q4 grew 3%; international grew 7% for the year and 25% in Q4. Management attributed the year's shortfall to JJM funding delays, a foundry ERP transition, and a Rs 389 mn labour-code charge classified as exceptional. Order books grew strongly: domestic Rs 24.680 bn (+30%) and international Rs 14.808 bn (+21%).

segments.name: Domestic (standalone)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs 28.281 bn (-3%); Q4 Rs 9.091 bn (+3%). Order growth led by building and construction, marine and defence, oil and gas, power and water; JJM is about 4-5% of revenue but hit water-sector shipments.

segments.name: International - SPP UK
segments.commentary: EBITDA fell from Rs 95 crore to Rs 58.1 crore (Rs 37 crore drop), driven by a shift from high-margin services to products as UK industrial customers idled on power prices above Rs 30/unit.

segments.name: International - SPP US
segments.commentary: Revenue about Rs 540 crore versus Rs 300 crore in FY22; about 35% from fire pumps and 25% from data centres. EBITDA down about Rs 3 crore per management.

segments.name: International - other entities
segments.commentary: Dutch, South African and other entities grew; South Africa margin % lower but absolute EBITDA higher. Management said Q4 was a slower first quarter for some entities due to prior-year spillover timing.

guidance_outlook: Management will strive for double-digit revenue growth in FY27 in both domestic and international businesses, but cited war and gas-supply risks.
SPP UK margins expected to realign toward the target level by roughly the calendar Q3 2026, with full-year margins targeted back to desired levels.
Labour-code impact of Rs 389 mn in FY26 (Rs 258 mn in Q4) treated as exceptional; estimates may be revised as rules are notified.
Final dividend of Rs 7 per Rs 2 share (350%) recommended, subject to AGM approval.
Management expects JJM-related disruption to ease over the next few quarters; AMP8 inquiries are expected to convert from next quarter.
capex_capacity: Foundry ERP (SAP) transition at Kirloskarvadi caused temporary disruption; management says the system has largely stabilised.
Company has five foundries; the largest was the focus this year, and in-house electricity capacity was added to hedge gas shortages.
Eight US data-centre packages were on the shop floor at the US plant as of the call.
Nuclear: full-scale primary heat transport pump prototype is to be delivered to NPCIL on schedule; budgetary quotes given for all pump types; Bharat SMR (200 MW) quotes sought.
demand_pricing: Standalone order inflow growth came from building and construction, marine and defence, oil and gas, power (coal and nuclear), and water and irrigation.
Company says it earns premiums against multinationals on lifecycle cost and efficiency, and enforces advance payment or LC for small and medium pumps; retail sold on cash.
Management says it can pass on raw-material price rises; Hormuz-related disruption raised costs.

SPP US competes with Amstel, Taco, Grundfos and Xylem in data-centre cooling; management says it is not cheaper but offers plug-and-play containerised packages with 18-24 month data-centre lead times.
US distributors rose to about 46 from 12 four years ago; roughly 10 states have no coverage.

qa_highlights.question: Where are the strong standalone orders coming from, and what else is disrupting execution beyond JJM?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth from building and construction, marine and defence, oil and gas, power and water. Execution was hit by the foundry ERP transition and JJM fund-release delays at the state level.

qa_highlights.question: Why did international margins fall despite strong order inflow?
qa_highlights.answer: Alok Kirloskar said the SPP UK mix shifted away from services because UK industrial customers idled on power prices above Rs 30/unit. Margins are expected to realign by about calendar Q3 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Would FY26 have grown at double digits without the disruptions?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Kirloskar said Q4 sales exceeded last year's Q4 and growth should resume, but war and gas uncertainty remain. He declined to give a precise FY27 figure beyond striving for double digits.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nuclear opportunity and timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Company has indigenously designed primary-side pumps, with budgetary quotes given. Orders are expected step by step as NPCIL and DAE constraints clear; SMR prototype orders are expected once the design is finalised.

qa_highlights.question: How diversified is the US business, and what is the 3-year plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Fire is about 35% of US business and data centres about 25%; the rest is municipal and booster packages. Focus is HVAC, municipal markets and AMP8-style programmes.

qa_highlights.question: Why did profit fall across international entities in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Alok Kirloskar said Q4 is seasonally slower for some entities due to prior-year spillover, and that year-on-year all entities except SPP UK improved.

risks_watch: SPP UK service mix and margin recovery timing (calendar Q3 2026 target).
JJM second-phase tendering and state-level fund release; no meaningful tendering pickup yet.
Geopolitical shocks (Middle East war, gas and fertiliser supply), with management citing cost pressure.
Foundry ERP stabilisation and dispatch conversion of the Rs 24.7 bn domestic order book.
Data-centre demand, where management acknowledged a mild US delay; ECA financing is a dependency.
Further labour-code revisions could change the Rs 389 mn exceptional charge.
summary.management_tone: Confident on order book, nuclear and data-centre opportunities, but cautious and evasive on FY27 growth, citing wars and gas shortages. Management was candid that FY26 margins and volumes were hit by SPP UK mix and operational transitions. Several questions on order-book breakdown and aftersales share were declined.
key_quotes: the double-digit growth that we expected was actually impacted by the first quarter, second quarter and third quarter.
So we do expect that we will get back to that level.
We're not cheaper, but we changed the model before to a modular model, and we provide a container system to them.

adds.what: Eight US data-centre packages on the shop floor at US plant (order-driven build, not new capacity announced)

growth.why: Management will "strive" for double-digit FY27 revenue growth in both domestic and international, backed by domestic order book of Rs 24.68 bn (+30%) and international order book of Rs 14.81 bn (+21%), but no specific capacity additions were quantified and war/gas risks were flagged.
